docs.title: ScopeTrace
docs.text: siddiqsoft::ScopeTrace is a header-only C++23 RAII scope logger designed for execution tracing, performance measurement, and nesting depth visualization.

docs.title: Key Highlights
docs.text:
• Zero-Boilerplate Tracing: Automatically record function name, file path, and line numbers using std::source_location.
  • Nesting Level Tracking: Indents nested scope execution trees dynamically using thread-local scope depth.
  • Structured Console Logging: Methods for msg(), warn(), err(), and exp() with depth indentation and ANSI colors.
  • C++23 Native Support: Leverages std::format, std::println, and std::ostream.

docs.title: Quick Example
docs.text:
#include <iostream>
#include <siddiqsoft/ScopeTrace.hpp>

void process_request()
{
    siddiqsoft::ScopeTrace scope("process_request");
    scope.msg("Parsing incoming payload...");
    // Work executed here...
}

int main()
{
    siddiqsoft::ScopeTrace scope("main");
    process_request();
    return 0;
}

docs.title: ScopeTrace Class API Reference
docs.text:
Header: <siddiqsoft/ScopeTrace.hpp>

namespace siddiqsoft {
    class ScopeTrace;
}

siddiqsoft::ScopeTrace is a modern C++23 RAII scope logging utility that measures duration, tracks nesting levels, records source locations, and formats diagnostic messages.

docs.title: explicit ScopeTrace(std::string_view sn, const std::source_location& sl = std::source_location::current())
docs.text:
Constructs a scope logger with the specified scope name sn and current source location sl. Increments the thread-local nesting depth.

  • sn: Scope name or contextual identifier.
  • sl: Source location (defaults to std::source_location::current()).

docs.title: ~ScopeTrace() noexcept
docs.text: Destructor. Decrements the thread-local nesting depth. In debug builds (DEBUG / _DEBUG), logs a scope completion message with elapsed duration (in microseconds) to std::cerr.

docs.title: Copy & Move Operations
docs.text: Copy construction, move construction, copy assignment, and move assignment operators are explicitly = delete.

docs.title: static size_t& current_depth() noexcept
docs.text: Accesses the thread-local scope depth counter. Returns a reference to the current thread's nesting depth index (size_t).

docs.title: [[nodiscard]] auto elapsed() const noexcept
docs.text: Calculates and returns the duration (std::chrono::system_clock::duration) elapsed since the ScopeTrace instance was constructed.

docs.title: [[nodiscard]] size_t depth() const noexcept
docs.text: Returns the nesting depth index of this scope instance (0 for top-level scopes).

docs.title: [[nodiscard]] const std::source_location& location() const noexcept
docs.text: Returns the std::source_location object captured at construction.

docs.title: [[nodiscard]] std::string_view name() const noexcept
docs.text: Returns the scope name string view passed at construction.

docs.title: template <typename... Args> void warn(std::format_string<Args...> fmt, Args&&... args)
docs.text: Formats and outputs a warning message to std::cerr (colored yellow) prefixed by the depth-indented scope name.

docs.title: template <typename... Args> void err(std::format_string<Args...> fmt, Args&&... args)
docs.text: Formats and outputs an error message to std::cerr (colored red) prefixed by the depth-indented scope name.

docs.title: void exp(const std::exception& e)
docs.text: Outputs caught exception details (typeid(e).name() and e.what()) to std::cerr (colored bold red) prefixed by the depth-indented scope name.

docs.title: template <typename... Args> void msg(std::format_string<Args...> fmt, Args&&... args)
docs.text: In debug builds (DEBUG / _DEBUG), formats and outputs an informational message to std::cerr prefixed by the depth-indented scope name.

docs.title: template <typename charT = char> [[nodiscard]] auto to_string() const
docs.text: Formats the scope log as a string containing line indentation, source location, function name, scope name, and elapsed duration in microseconds.

docs.title: friend std::ostream& operator<<(std::ostream& os, const ScopeTrace& src)
docs.text: Stream insertion operator. Writes src.to_string<char>() to the standard output stream os.

docs.title: Basic Usage Example
docs.text:
This example demonstrates how to use siddiqsoft::ScopeTrace for scope tracing, nested scope timing, warning and error logging, exception capture, and string formatting.

#include <iostream>
#include <thread>
#include <stdexcept>
#include <siddiqsoft/ScopeTrace.hpp>

void worker()
{
    siddiqsoft::ScopeTrace scope("worker");
    scope.msg("Worker starting task with ID={}", 42);

    std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(10));

    scope.warn("Resource usage reached {}%", 85);
}

void perform_operation()
{
    siddiqsoft::ScopeTrace scope("perform_operation");
    worker();

    try {
        throw std::runtime_error("Simulated failure in sub-system");
    }
    catch (const std::exception& e) {
        scope.exp(e);
    }
}

int main()
{
    siddiqsoft::ScopeTrace scope("main");
    scope.msg("Application initialization complete");

    perform_operation();

    // Stream formatting example
    std::cout << "Scope summary: " << scope << std::endl;

    return 0;
}

docs.title: Features Overview
docs.text: siddiqsoft::ScopeTrace provides a rich set of capabilities designed for modern C++ application tracing, performance profiling, and scope execution logging.

docs.title: Core Capabilities
docs.text:
• Scope Logging: Detailed explanation of RAII timing, location capture, depth tracking, and structured message logging.
  • Quick Reference: Handy cheat sheet for API usage patterns and options.
  • Security & Exception Model: Overview of exception guarantees, thread safety, and memory safety guarantees.

docs.title: Structured Console Logging
docs.text:
// Info log (in debug builds)
scope.msg("Processing item {} of {}", current, total);

// Warning log (yellow output)
scope.warn("Cache miss for key: {}", key);

// Error log (red output)
scope.err("Failed to open connection to host: {}", host);

// Exception log (red bold output)
try {
    // ...
} catch (const std::exception& e) {
    scope.exp(e);
}

docs.title: Formatting & Streaming
docs.text:
// Format as std::string
std::string formatted = scope.to_string();

// Stream insertion operator
std::cout << scope << std::endl;

docs.title: Scope Metrics & Nesting
docs.text:
// Elapsed time
auto duration = scope.elapsed();

// Instance nesting depth
size_t level = scope.depth();

// Current thread nesting depth counter
size_t thread_depth = siddiqsoft::ScopeTrace::current_depth();

docs.title: How RAII Scope Logging Works
docs.text:
siddiqsoft::ScopeTrace uses the C++ RAII pattern to measure scope execution duration and emit trace logs upon scope entry and exit.

#include <siddiqsoft/ScopeTrace.hpp>

void compute()
{
    siddiqsoft::ScopeTrace scope("compute_operation");
    // Code block execution...
} // Destruction logs completion status and elapsed duration automatically in debug builds

docs.title: Source Location
docs.text: Using std::source_location::current(), ScopeTrace captures caller details automatically: - Source file path (location().file_name()) - Line number (location().line()) - Enclosing function signature (location().function_name())

docs.title: Nesting Depth Tracking
docs.text:
ScopeTrace automatically tracks nested scopes using a thread-local counter (current_depth()), producing formatted visual indentation for hierarchical log trees:

[main.cpp:12] compute_operation took 150us
  [main.cpp:18] sub_stage took 40us

docs.title: In-Scope Logging Sinks
docs.text:
Within an active scope, you can output formatted contextual messages to std::cerr with depth indentation and ANSI color coding:

  • scope.msg("..."): Debug information (active in DEBUG / _DEBUG builds).
  • scope.warn("..."): Warning messages (colored yellow).
  • scope.err("..."): Error messages (colored red).
  • scope.exp(e): Formatted exception log (colored bold red with exception type and what()).

docs.title: Exception Safety
docs.text:
• noexcept Destructor Guarantee: siddiqsoft::ScopeTrace::~ScopeTrace() is explicitly declared noexcept to ensure safety during stack unwinding.
  • Exception Logging Utility: The scope.exp(const std::exception& e) method safe-prints exception types and messages to std::cerr without throwing exceptions.

docs.title: Thread Safety & Performance
docs.text:
• Zero-Lock Nesting Depth: Scope nesting depth is stored in thread_local state (current_depth()), requiring zero lock contention or synchronization overhead across concurrent threads.
  • Header-Only Efficiency: Small, lightweight header-only implementation with minimal overhead.
